name: Blackpink
notes: Trap-EDM idol pop organised around an instrumental drop-chorus, flagged in the research as a K-pop sub-lane. The Lane line names the trap sections first and gives them the half-time class, so `halfTime` is true at `halftime_3`; the big-room drop survives as `fourOnFloorInChorus`. The kit is the entry's: "sparse half-time trap kick with 32nd hat rolls under the verses, then a big-room kick pattern in the drop; the signature device is a bass drop placed immediately before the chorus." So the kick density is the sparsest of the K-pop group at 1—4, the roll vocabulary is 32nd-dominant at the highest `freqPerBar` in this batch, `impact` and `riser` lead the perc lanes, and the arrangement carries a very deep `dropOutBeats` for the pre-chorus bass drop. The 808 is authored because the entry names it — "heavy 808 sub with pitch glides in the verses; a distorted big-room sub locked to the kick in the drop" — as `counter_riff` with the highest `slideProb` in this section and `medium` distortion, with the big-room sub remaining the bassline on a kick mirror. Harmony is "4-bar minor loops" with "Middle-Eastern-inflected scale colour on several singles", which is why `harmonic_minor` and `phrygian_dominant` carry real weight. The melody block encodes the vocal casting the entry calls the parameter — "a soprano lead, a mezzo-soprano, and two rappers, so register contrast is built into the arrangement" — as the widest melody register in this batch and a `densityPerBar` that spans rap and sung. The hook itself is the counter: "a chanted or instrumental chorus rather than a sung one — the hook is frequently a synth or vocal-chop riff", so `answer_lick` carries top weight at a very high density ratio. ⚠ `confidence` is medium and the research says "tempo and harmonic bands are genre-derived": every drum probability, the humanize numbers, the harmonic weights and `bpm.mode` 115 (the midpoint of the stated 90—140 band) are INFERRED. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 966/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** The 1-bar value came out of `melody.phraseBars`, which is now [2,4] weighted [4,2]. `generators::melody` writes a phrase's rhythm **once** and reuses it for every repeat, so a 1-bar phrase gives the whole clip one bar of rhythmic entropy — and the counter, whose onsets are read off the lead's, inherits that ceiling. Distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "4-bar minor loops; palette is brass-and-supersaw stabs plus plucked ethnic-instrument samples. Toplines alternate bold rapped verses with a powerfully sung pre-chorus and a chanted or instrumental chorus rather than a sung one — the hook is frequently a synth or vocal-chop riff.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
